scope: Shorten shared heap metadata ownership during large free/realloc-tail poisoning and permitted VM tail work.

implementation.owner: Mandatory kernel allocator; private memory/heap/release.rs shares the existing Control/owner4 and task unwind admission. No public API, separate resource registry or new module.
implementation.blocks: Large blocks and split realloc tails get used+retiring boundary tags and a monotonic exact ticket. They remain outside bins and neighbour coalescence while the complete original0xDD payload fill runs without owner4. Revalidate size/header/footer/ticket before accounting and normal coalescence/publication. Small or outer-owner frees keep the original locked fill. Ticket exhaustion also keeps that path.
implementation.tails: The existing GROWTH serialization holds the exact retired range/start/bytes/pressure tuple until actual VM completion. Existing free bins remain usable; growth and other tail completions cannot reuse it. Failed/partial uncommit preserves the original retry anchor. Actual completion/counters precede publication and waiter wake; original task unwind admission spans the wake.
implementation.permissions: CPU-only poisoning touches resident kernel-heap payload and adds no wait. Tail owner handoff requires the original saved IF, no outer memory/runtime owner and the existing task wait permission. Otherwise preserve the original locked VM path. No mutable Control borrow spans fill, VM, scheduler or wake calls.
implementation.preserved: All size classes, alignment, boundary tags, coalescence, adaptive growth, retention/pressure policy, full functional poison, original error classifications and232byte Stats ABI. Realloc copy path and public deallocation signatures remain. Kernelheap is not demand-page evictable; VM pager reclaim is window6 only.

Entire heap/release/policy and task unwind sources, only heap BASE rebound for a Linux host mmap. Owner/IRQ/scheduler/VM backend are models, not native concurrency evidence.
